The Full Governing Body at Cornerstone meets six times per academic year.
Extraordinary Full Governing Body meetings can be called, should the need arise.
In addition, governors serve on one or more of the following Governing Body Committees, which convene at least once per term:
Resources, Pay and Personnel
Meeting minutes for the Full Governing Body as well as each of the Committees can be obtained from the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: In Year applications - Cornerstone C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
In year applications
How to apply
You need to complete an in-year application form which is available to be completed either online or in other ways:
You can apply online here:
Applying for a school place in-year | Hampshire County Council (hants.gov.uk)
Requesting the form from any Hampshire primary, junior or secondary school
Requesting a form is posted to you from the County Admissions Team (County Admissions Team, Children’s Services Department, The Castle, Winchester, Hampshire, SO23 8UG)
Completed applications should be returned to the County Admissions Team at the address above.
When should I expect to receive the decision letter?
Parents should allow 10 work days for their application to be processed.
A letter will then be emailed to you advising of the school place being offered to your child.
Once you receive your letter offering your child a place you will need to confirm your decision in writing to your present school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Becoming a governor - Cornerstone C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Becoming a governor
Do you want to play a key part in helping support children, teachers, and leaders at Cornerstone Primary School?
New Governor expression of interest form.
Governors play an important part in shaping a school, keeping leaders accountable, and helping to create a learning environment that is safe, effective and enjoyable for all children.
We are looking for individuals who are interested in giving a bit of their time to their local community, and making a big difference for the next generation of pupils and teachers.
No particular experience is needed – in fact, we welcome people of all ages, backgrounds, and walks of life to contribute to the rewarding work we do as a governing body for Cornerstone.
What does a governor do?
The role of the governing body is to ensure the school maintains high standards of achievement for all its children. It monitors these key areas:
VisionEnsuring there is a clear vision, ethos, and strategic direction.
AccountabilityHolding executive leaders to account for the educational performance at the school, and the performance management of staff.
Financial ResponsibilityOverseeing the financial performance of the organisation and making sure its money is well spent.
Upholding the Christian foundation of the school in accordance with the CofE Trust Deed.
How much time does it require to be a governor?
In a normal academic year, the Full Governing Body at Cornerstone meets six times. The meetings typically take place between 6pm and 8pm on a weekday evening, in the school staff room. There is the option to join some governor meetings remotely via Microsoft Teams, if a governor is unable to attend in person.
In addition, governors serve on one (or more) Governing Body Committee, which meets at least once per term. They are:
School ImprovementThis committee is responsible for a wide range of areas that relate to the quality of education, the welfare of pupils and staff, and innovation in the classroom.
Resources, Pay and PersonnelThis committee handles all aspects of managing school facilities, spending, recruitment, IT and infrastructure, and any other financial management issues. .
Between meetings, governors are encouraged to visit the school to speak to staff and pupils, take part in collective worship, watch performances, or to volunteer at sports or cultural activities. This is both rewarding and fun for everyone involved, it allows governors to keep a fresh view on what’s happening at the school, and ultimately helps them make good decisions.
All governors are also offered free, self-paced training on a wide range of topics such as safeguarding, finance, policies, health and wellbeing, and much more.
What types of governors are there?
At Cornerstone, we have seven types of governors.
Parent GovernorA parent governor is a parent, grandparent, or carer of a pupil enrolled at Cornerstone Primary School. They represent the perspective of parents and pupils, highlighting any specific needs they observe in the context of how the school meets the needs of parents and children.
Staff GovernorAny member of staff employed by Cornerstone Primary School can be a staff governor. They represent the perspective as a staff member and offer insights of the staff experience.
Foundation GovernorFoundation governors are endorsed and approved by the Diocese of Portsmouth. They are responsible for ensuring that the Christian ethos of the school is encouraged and reflected in its policies, the curriculum, and day-to-day life.
Local Authority GovernorA local authority governor represents the local council, ensuring the school meets educational standards and serves its community effectively. They focus on fostering improvement while upholding the school’s vision, values, and statutory responsibilities.
Co-Opted GovernorA co-opted governor is a person appointed to a school’s governing board to help the school succeed. They are chosen by the governing board because they have a set of skills that allows them to contribute to the school’s success.
Ex-Officio GovernorThe ex-officio governor at Cornerstone Primary is the vicar of Hope Church, Whiteley. Their role is to contribute to the board by providing a Christian perspective on matters relating to the school, as well as to offer guidance and pastoral care to the board of governors.
Who can be a governor?
Anyone aged 18 or over can apply to be a governor at Cornerstone Primary. You don’t need any experience of working with children, but we welcome candidates who take an active interest in education and welfare of children and teachers. Beyond that, your own background and experience will no doubt offer valuable contributions to the board.
Following a successful application, you will be DBS-checked and introduced to the work of the governing board through an induction programme. The term of office is four years.
To apply to become a member of the Board of Governors at Cornerstone Primary School, please complete this form (to be added shortly) and we’ll connect with you as soon as possible.
Thank you for considering becoming a governor – you can make a real difference!
